rationale: Lycopolitan plural — likely reflex of ϩⲟⲩⲣⲉ/ϩⲟⲟⲩⲗⲉ 'miscarriage, abortion.' The Manichaean myth of archonic abortions falling to earth before Adam/Eve's fashioning is the controlling context. Reduplicated/altered form ⲍⲟⲩⲍⲉ may reflect dialectal phonology.

Greek loanword ἀνδριάς 'statue, image of a man.' Manichaean technical term for the eschatological Last Statue — the final form of redeemed light at the consummation of the cosmos. Standard alongside the Pillar of Glory and the Great Mind in Manichaean eschatology.
Greek loanword ἐλπίς 'hope' with Lycopolitan ⲍ-prefix. Restored across lines 25-26 as the gift Jesus gave to Adam — a standard Manichaean teaching.

Lycopolitan reflex of ϫⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'draw, set in array, prepare.' In this passage paired antithetically with ⲥⲱⲍⲣⲉ 'drive down' to express the cosmic separation: drawing the light upward, driving the error downward.
Nominalization of ⲥⲱⲣⲙ̄ 'go astray.' Native Coptic term for what Greek ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ names — the cosmic principle of error/wandering, here driven down to the Deep by the Third Ambassador.
Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲉ/ϩⲉⲉⲓⲉ 'to fall.' Used here of the abortions falling downward.
Greek loanword ἀγών — the cosmic contest/struggle from which the First Man is brought up. Standard Manichaean term for the primordial battle.
